title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software

layers.name: Foundational Understanding
concepts: Design patterns are proven solutions to recurring problems
Each pattern has Problem → Solution → Consequences
layers.mental_model: Patterns are tested best practices organized by purpose

layers.name: Pattern Recognition
concepts: Identify when a problem matches a pattern
layers.mental_model: Each pattern solves a specific class of problems with known trade-offs

layers.name: SOLID Principles Application
layers.mental_model: Design patterns are concrete implementations of SOLID principles

layers.name: Design Decision Making
layers.mental_model: Patterns are tools, not rules. Use them judiciously based on context.

layers.name: Team Communication & Architecture
layers.mental_model: Patterns are a language for expressing design intent and architectural decisions

stage_1_identify.approach: Is this an object creation, composition, or interaction problem?

stage_4_evaluate_tradeoffs.approach: Benefits vs. Learning curve vs. Context mismatch

stage_5_decide.approach: Start simple, apply pattern only if needed

assumptions: Patterns address real recurring problems in software design
Pattern knowledge improves code quality and communication
Trade-offs must be evaluated before applying patterns
Context and simplicity matter more than pattern purity
Understanding principles matters more than memorizing mechanics
biases_to_avoid: Cargo cult programming: Applying patterns without understanding
Premature optimization: Building for future problems that may not exist
Context blindness: Applying patterns that don't fit the specific situation

alternative_perspectives.contrast: Some behavioral patterns become trivial with functions (Strategy → higher-order functions)
Patterns should reflect domain concepts, not just implementation details
Start simple, apply patterns incrementally as needs emerge
